title: A day from London
excerpt: Leave Charing Cross at dawn and travel for twelve hours. In 1750 that reached 5% of Great Britain; in the 1830s 19%; by rail in 1850 at least 47%; in 1910 at least 72%; today 97%. I rebuilt five eras of roads and railways to map the edge of the day.
seo_description: How much of Great Britain could you reach in a day from London? 5% in 1750, 97% today. Roads and railways of five eras.
header_alt: Title card on cream paper reading 'A day from London' beside two maps of Great Britain coloured by hours of travel from London, a small patch around London in 1750 and almost the whole island today.
